newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares creep up early on retail interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares creep up early on retail interest.

text.p: The Singapore stock market inched a shade higher on Thursday, finding more support from retail interest, but blue chip demand was subdued, dealers said.
"There's some speculative element on the retail side which will continue to play up the small issues," said one brokerage dealer who added that institutional action was slow.
At 0255 GMT, Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials index was up 3.33 points at 2,246.59 on a relatively active turnover of 96 million shares.
The index was seen supported by broad interest in selected electronic, manufacturing issues and some blue chips.
But overall sentiment remained mixed after corrections in New York, Hong Kong and Tokyo overnight, and profit taking pressure upon recent gains.
Leading the gainers were City Development, up Singapore $0.30 to $10.40, and DBS Land up $0.20 at $5.40.
Creative Technology pared Wednesday's takings, down $0.60 at $15.20, hurt by reports of advances in software by Intel. Some said the new technology may affect multimedia companies.
Technology-related SM Summit Holdings was again most traded with 11.64 million units, up $0.05 to $0.65.
